messages:
raj: Quick postmortem from today's perf sprint — p99 spikes on /generate are back after the kernel roll. Flamegraph link: https://internal.perf/redwood/flames/1751456789 :link:
perf-bot: Profiling run completed. Top offenders: variable-kernel-selection (37%), KV-cache miss handling (22%), tool-caller sync wait (14%). Full report uploaded.
lina: saw this too locally. The new fused-attn kernel falls back to slow path for sequence_length > 2048, which some long-prompt customers hit.
ben: microbatch side: our autoscaler pushed microbatch size to 16 to hit throughput targets; that increases tail when samples have longer prompts. p95 OK, p99 bad.
olivia: also noticed a class of requests that do tool-calls in the middle of generation (user prompt triggers a structured tool call loop). Those end up invalidating KV cache and cause re-encode + full attention re-compute.
raj: notes from flamegraph: the matmul kernel times jump massively at ~2k tokens. We should confirm kernel selection threshold and fallback path.
lina: confirmed — kernel selector checks block_size and dtype heuristics, but it only considers static context length; it doesn't account for runtime prompt extension from tool calls. Patch idea: re-evaluate kernel choice post-tool-call or maintain a fast-path for incremental KV extend.
ben: suggestion: lower microbatch target for routes with high prompt-length variance. We can add a per-route microbatch cap in routing policy to keep p99 bounds.
olivia: sample log snippet of a problematic trace:
```
[req=abcd] prompt_tokens=1800 generated=350 tool_call=start
[req=abcd] tool_resolve time=75ms -> appended 0 tokens, start re-gen
[req=abcd] kv_miss=true chosen_kernel=fused-attn-fallback
matmul_ms=180 avg=22
```
raj: that kv_miss=true line is interesting — why is KV missed after tool_return? Should be appending to KV, not rebuilding.
lina: root cause: our incremental-kv code assumes single-threaded append without interleaving; tool-caller runs on the same loop and sometimes re-allocates the KV buffer when the runtime does a small memcpy for tool outputs. That triggers a pointer-change and the cache indexing logic treats it as cold.
ben: ops mitigation: conservative approach — after tool-call return mark request as "kv-hot" and prefer kernel with stable indexing. Or avoid microbatch coalescing for these sessions.
olivia: long-term: add a lightweight KV-stability token to the request metadata so kernel selector can make better decision (skip slow fallback if token present). Also add histogram bucketing by effective context length (including expected tool output).
raj: action items: (1) lina to PR small kernel-selector fix to re-evaluate post-tool-call, (2) ben to add per-route microbatch cap and experiment with 8->12, (3) olivia to add KV-stability flag and instrument counts. I'll coordinate a canary with reduced microbatch for high-variance routes.
lina: will open PR and add unit tests covering tool-call-induced realloc.
ben: will push a routing-policy change to beta tomorrow.
olivia: I'll add metrics: kv_stability.count, tool_interleaved.regen_count, p99_by_route.
raj: thanks — let's sync tomorrow after the canary. :thumbsup:
